title: Studio Tricks
objective: After this level you can explain what studio effects like Auto-Tune do.
summary: Auto-Tune moves a sung note to the nearest semitone: a quiet fix, or a robot voice when pushed, as on Cher's Believe (1998). Studios add reverb; a drier voice seems closer.

cards.headline: Cher's robot voice came from a tool built to hide mistakes.
cards.body: On her 1998 hit "Believe," Cher's voice leaps from note to note like a machine. It was the first commercial recording to show off Auto-Tune's side effects on purpose. The tool was designed to fix singing quietly, and its inventor came from the oil business.

cards.headline: From oil fields to vocal booths
cards.body: Andy Hildebrand spent 1976 to 1989 interpreting seismic data for the oil industry. Later, his company Antares released Auto-Tune. It detects the pitch of each sung note and moves it to the nearest semitone: the smallest step on a keyboard, from one key to the very next, as you saw in Level 7. A slightly flat note gets nudged back into tune.

cards.headline: Invisible fix or robot effect
cards.body: Used gently, pitch correction tidies a vocal and you never notice. Push it hard and the voice leaps from note to note while staying perfectly, unnaturally in tune: the "Believe" sound. Engineers realized the side effect could be a style. Today both uses, the quiet fix and the obvious robot, are common in recorded music.

mascot.line: A bug, a feature, or a style? In music, sometimes all three.

cards.headline: Reverb: a room in a box
cards.body: Reverberation is sound that lingers after its source stops, built from reflections bouncing around a space. Studios often record in dry rooms lined with absorbent material, then add reverb afterward with metal plates, springs or digital algorithms. The balance sets the scene: the stronger the dry sound, the closer the singer seems. A voice recorded in a tiny booth can end up sounding like it's in a grand hall.

learned: Auto-Tune moves notes to the nearest semitone
Subtle, it corrects; pushed hard, it's a robot voice
Cher's Believe (1998) made the effect famous

questions.prompt: What does Auto-Tune do to a sung note?

options.label: Moves its pitch to the nearest semitone
Adds echoes to make it sound like a big hall
Makes it louder without changing pitch
Loops it like a drum break

questions.explanation: Auto-Tune detects the pitch and moves it to the nearest true semitone.

questions.prompt: An engineer wants a vocal to sound closer to the listener. What should they do with reverb?

options.label: Add much more reverb
options.rationale: More reverb makes it seem farther away.

options.label: Push Auto-Tune to its fastest setting
options.rationale: That changes pitch behavior, not distance.

options.label: Use less reverb, keeping the sound drier
Record it in the biggest room available
options.rationale: A big room adds more reflections.

questions.explanation: The stronger the dry sound compared with the reverb, the closer the voice seems.

questions.prompt: Auto-Tune snaps notes to the nearest semitone. In Level 7's terms, what is a semitone?

options.label: A note twice the frequency of another
A tone that lasts half a beat
options.rationale: A semitone is about pitch, not time.

options.label: The step from one keyboard key to the very next

questions.explanation: A semitone is the smallest step on a keyboard, key to next key, black or white.
